question: Blackstone's ratio: jailing an innocent is ten times worse than freeing a guilty person. Above what chance of guilt should juries convict, in per cent?
move: Put a price on each kind of mistake before choosing how sure to be.
trap: Turning ten to one into 90% instead of ten in eleven.
hint: Weigh each mistake by its cost: at the tipping point, the two expected costs are equal.
steps: Acquitting risks freeing the guilty: chance p, cost 1.
Convicting risks jailing an innocent: chance 1 − p, cost 10.
Convict once p is greater than 10 × (1 − p), that is once 11p > 10.
reference: Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book IV, chapter 27, 1769; Volokh, n Guilty Men, University of Pennsylvania Law Review 146, 1997
